findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights to admins that only have the 'view' scope on all groups
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it treats the `view` scope on the aggregate "Groups" resource as sufficient for manage. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an admin who was only granted an all-groups *view* permission can create top-level groups. Compare with the group-scoped variant `canManage(GroupModel)` (line 79) which correctly checks only `MANAGE`, and with `UserPermissionsV2`, where manage never falls back to view. The javadoc added in `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` documents the same wrong behaviour. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization Resource IDs, not group IDs, and never finds per-group resources
findings.body:
The V2 implementation collects `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authz `Resource` id) into the returned set, but all callers treat the returned values as group IDs: `UsersResource.searchForUser()`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser()` put them into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` passes them to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. In FGAP V2 the per-object resource *name* is the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`), so the ids returned here never match any group and the user query is restricted to a non-existent group – an admin that has `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups gets an empty user list. The same wrong value is also passed back into `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` on line 122, which resolves resources via `resourceStore.findByName()`, so the per-resource lookup always misses and silently falls back to evaluating the aggregate "Groups" resource.
In addition, `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` can only return the aggregate "Groups" resource, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates per-object resources without calling `setType()`. Consequently per-group view-members permissions are never reported, which makes `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` return 0 for such admins while the user list endpoint still returns users (count and list disagree). V1 (`GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`) does this correctly by using `resource.getName()`.

findings.title: NPE when the aggregate "Groups" resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In `hasPermission()`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) the resource server exists but `supportsAuthorizationSchema()` is false, e.g. a realm where the admin-permissions client was created once and `adminPermissionsEnabled` was later turned off, and (b) the "Groups" resource does not exist in the resource server (realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this resource type was added – `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` only runs when the client is first created). In both cases any group/user listing by an admin without `view-users`/`query-groups` roles ends in a NullPointerException and a 500 response instead of a plain "denied".

findings.title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
findings.body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so the newly added "Groups" aggregate resource and the new scopes (`manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members`) are only created for realms that enable admin permissions after this change. For a realm that already enabled FGAP V2 with an earlier build: creating any Groups scope permission fails because `getOrCreateResource()` (line 125) throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when a schema scope is missing from the resource server, and group permission evaluation hits the missing aggregate resource (see `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`). Either a migration that adds missing scopes/resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions clients or an idempotent re-initialisation is needed.

findings.title: Evaluated permissions are not filtered to the requested resource (inconsistent with UserPermissionsV2)
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` iterates all `Permission` objects returned by `root.evaluatePermission(...)` and grants access as soon as any of them carries one of the expected scopes. `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` (line 123 of that file) deliberately guards this with `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. Without that guard, any permission the policy engine returns for a resource other than the one being evaluated (e.g. scope-only or resource-type expanded permissions) would grant access on the wrong group. The two implementations should use the same rule.

findings.title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers refers to canManageMembership
findings.body: The javadoc added for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" – it is a copy of the javadoc of `requireManageMembership` and documents the wrong predicate; the method actually delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Since these two scopes (`manage-membership` vs `manage-members`) grant very different privileges, wrong documentation on this security API is misleading for implementors. Also note that the javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set`, and the permission it actually checks is view-members/manage-members, not `view`.

findings.title: No coverage for all-groups view-members, for the users count endpoint, or for the group members endpoint
findings.body: The new test class only exercises per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` through `users().search(...)`, which happens to work even when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns nothing (the search then runs unrestricted and is filtered per user). Missing cases that would have caught the broken `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`: (1) an *all-groups* `view-members`/`manage-members` permission followed by `users().search(...)` (currently returns nothing because an authz resource id is used as a group id filter), (2) `users().count()` for an admin whose only visibility comes from group member permissions (currently returns 0 while `search` returns users), and (3) `groups().group(id).members()` which is guarded by the new `requireViewMembers` path.

findings.title: Removal of the global view short-circuit makes group listing evaluate policies per group
findings.body: `getGroups()` previously computed `boolean canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and only evaluated `canView(group)` per group when the global check failed; the same hoisting was removed in `GroupResource.getSubGroups()`. With FGAP V2, `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group)` performs a resource lookup by name plus a full policy evaluation for every group in the stream (and in `getSubGroups` the filter is applied over all subgroups before pagination). For a policy-based admin holding an all-groups view permission this turns one evaluation into one per listed group, which is the main use case of the new feature. Consider keeping the single global check as a short-circuit.
